summary: Repository hygiene is strong. Local, origin/main and VPS share HEAD ab1b264 with identical tree hash fbece21 and content hash 876449f9, porcelain is clean on both ends, CI run 38792617932 concluded success across all three jobs (Windows 30 passed, unit 130/0/0/0, vox 67/0/0/0), and ghost_scan exits 0. The increment still cannot be approved because the evidence packet contradicts itself on the primary objectives. (1) The S05 live runtime proof exits 1 with AttributeError in core/paths.py:29, yet Section 7 claims 'live runtime execution on VPS (exit 0)'. That is an unverified claim contradicted by raw evidence, a direct Rule 121/127 violation. (2) The Daily Quota Guard is currently blocking today's production. /var/vf/locks/b1_daily_lock/EN_2026-10-16.json was sealed EXHAUSTED_TODAY at 17:42 UTC, which is 00:42 VN, by pre-policy code (scan_count=15). The live dry-run confirms 'EN: SKIP (EXHAUSTED_TODAY) — VN Date: 2026-10-16'. The Minimum VN-Hour Policy exists in code but was never reconciled against live state, so the 06:00 VN window it claims to protect is already lost. (3) Production state under /var/vf/locks was polluted by test or CLI runs: 27 suppressions and two EXHAUSTED locks came from PIDs the Worker attributes to 'pre-deploy test runs'. That proves test isolation was absent at the time, and the next legitimate alert will carry a misleading '(+27 suppressed)' suffix. (4) Several lock-engine defects violate the fail-closed contract: a fail-open IN_PROGRESS branch, one-shot fail-closed on corruption, a non-exclusive stale-lock takeover race, and a tombstone reclaim that can destroy a live lock. Empty `except Exception: pass` blocks also remain. (5) Scope and Rule 125 issues: cleanup_corrupt_quarantines is duplicated, hhtech_reasoner.py was rewritten wholesale (580/580) with unverifiable content, test_align_adversarial.py (210 lines) was deleted, and unrelated AVF-VOX-001 work is mixed into the range.

Production state remediation, which requires explicit operator confirmation under Rule 137 because it modifies live lock state: quarantine-rename (do not delete) /var/vf/locks/b1_daily_lock/EN_2026-10-16.json and reset the test-origin suppression counter in /var/vf/locks/alert_cooldown.json. Unify _atomic_write_json and _write_cooldown_data (uuid tmp name, fsync, raise on failure) and cleanup_corrupt_quarantines into a single shared core module (Rule 125).
Resolve episode roots through core.paths instead of hardcoded /var/vf and /root paths. Determine completion from manifest content (a completed status field), not file mtime.

Add a regression test replaying Incident 1 → Incident 2: Gate 1 sent, task committed, B3 crash, then a second same-day invocation. It must assert that B1 skips. Define and document the lock state written on a B3 crash.

Justify the deletion of tests/vox/test_align_adversarial.py and ALLOW_SYNTHETIC_ALIGNMENT by naming the replacement tests that cover the same adversarial alignment boundaries against real word timelines (Rule 120/134), or restore them.

Prove B3 module resolution under the exact cron environment (same user, cwd, PYTHONPATH, interpreter as /var/vf/logs/daily_cron_b1_b2.log) and identify the commit that fixed 'No module named orchestrator.run_pipeline'.
Reconcile the VPS test count (85 vs 89), attach the untruncated pytest output, and extend the OCR scan to all changed Python files rather than 5.
Attach Telegram dispatch evidence (sendMessage log lines or message IDs) for the 15:41–17:42 UTC window to substantiate 'zero duplicate alerts'.
Split or annotate the commit range so TASK_1792069373 changes are separable from AVF-VOX-001 and tooling changes (Rule 124).

component_reviews.analysis: The stated root cause (s3_data never loaded) is plausible, and 3/3 unit tests pass via resolve_run_paths. However, the 19-line s05 diff and the 41-line core/paths.py diff are not included untruncated, so the fix cannot be line-verified (Rule 121). The mandated live execution exits 1: RunPaths.__init__ calls self.run_id.startswith() on a PosixPath. Either the live harness (boss_orchestrator.py:1278 emits 'from core.paths import RunPaths') passes a Path where str is required, or RunPaths lost type coercion in this increment. In both cases the Rule 127 proof failed. The report then claims exit 0, which is a fabricated success statement against raw evidence.

Fail-open paths exist. (a) If status == IN_PROGRESS and created_at_utc is missing or empty, the branch falls through with no return, and the function can return not_produced_yet. (b) Any unknown status string also falls through to fail-open. (c) A corrupt lock is quarantined and returns fail-closed once, but the quarantine removes the file, so the next cron tick sees no lock and crawls. Fail-closed is therefore one-shot, contradicting the module mandate and the operator alert text. (d) The registry loop uses a bare `except Exception: pass`. (e) Episode roots hardcode /var/vf/episodes and /root/video_factory/episodes instead of resolving through core.paths, a Rule 132 decoupling deviation. (f) Episode completion is inferred from run_manifest.json mtime rather than a completion status inside the manifest, so any touch or partial manifest seals the day. (g) It is not demonstrated that Incident 1 (Gate 1 sent, task committed, B3 crashed, no run_manifest) would have blocked the 15:29 VN redundant crawl. That incident is the motivating case for this task.

The initial O_CREAT|O_EXCL acquire is correct. Stale takeover is not exclusive. Two processes that both observe a stale IN_PROGRESS lock will both call _atomic_write_json and both return True, so mutual exclusion is broken exactly in the recovery path. _atomic_write_json names its tmp file with pid plus integer-second timestamp (collision-prone within one second), skips fsync, and returns False instead of raising. This is inconsistent with alert_cooldown._write_cooldown_data, which uses uuid tmp names, fsync, and raises. The corrupt-lock Telegram dispatch also swallows all errors with `except Exception: pass`, so an operator alert can fail silently.

The reclaim sequence has a TOCTOU hole. It reads raw, checks the PID is dead, then os.rename(lock_file, tombstone). If another process reclaims and a third acquires between the read and the rename, this process renames away a live holder's lock. The post-rename check `tomb_content == raw` detects the mismatch but only skips the log line, then unlinks the tombstone anyway and does not restore it. Two holders can then run concurrently. The fix is to restore the tombstone on mismatch (rename back with O_EXCL semantics) or to compare-and-reclaim using the token. The `except Exception: if isinstance(e, LockTimeoutError)` branch is dead code because LockTimeoutError is raised inside the sibling FileExistsError handler. The Windows is_pid_alive logic (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER only, fail-closed otherwise) is correct.

Single-lock check, increment, and reserve is correct, and the concurrency test passes. rollback_alert_reservation with previous_last_sent=None deletes the whole entry, which discards suppressions recorded by concurrent callers between reservation and rollback. It should restore the counter rather than delete. The trend_engine_b1.py integration (132 lines) is not shown, so the reserve → send → rollback-on-failure wiring around the Telegram call is not line-verified.

EN_2026-10-16.json was written at 2026-10-15T17:42 UTC (00:42 VN, 16 Oct) by PID 70545 with scan_count=15, and it is actively blocking EN today. EN_2026-10-15.json (PID 63430, 23:56 VN) and the 27 suppressions also came from non-production runs. The provenance claim that these were 'MCP pre-deploy test subprocesses before 6ec5964' is narrative only. No process log, command line, or commit timestamp is provided. Whatever the origin, the evidence shows tests wrote to production VF_STATE_DIR. The '0 duplicate alerts reached Telegram' claim is also unsupported, since no Telegram sendMessage log or bot API history is attached.

The /health endpoint now spawns `git rev-parse` on every request. This adds unbounded subprocess cost on what is likely an unauthenticated endpoint, so caching once per process is advised. The resolution order also flipped (git before env), which changes behavior in containers without .git, and the failure log was downgraded from warning to debug. The `request: Request` parameter was removed from call_llm with no Rule 138 caller or middleware impact evidence (auth, rate-limit, client-IP logging).

The 580-line removal and 580-line addition indicate a whole-file rewrite, most likely CRLF/LF churn. The diff is truncated, so content equivalence is unverified. The visible body carries pre-existing defects: two unreachable `return (...)` blocks after the history branch (orphaned elif conditions for tech_geopolitical and ancient_prehistory), a bare `except Exception: pass` in get_hhtech_key and _fetch_native_wiki_extract, and hardcoded topic and entity keyword lists (e.g. specific cases and companies) that conflict with Rule 128. The file is outside task scope and should not be in this range unless the change is proven byte-equivalent after normalization.

Coverage of the new modules is good: concurrency, timeout, tombstone, rollback, VN-hour policy, and retention are all tested. Evidence is inconsistent, though: the VPS header says '85 passed' while the summary says '89 passed', and the listing is truncated below 8%. tests/vox/test_align_adversarial.py (210 lines) was deleted along with ALLOW_SYNTHETIC_ALIGNMENT, with no Rule 139 justification showing that equivalent adversarial alignment coverage now exists against real Whisper output (Rule 120). No test covers stale-takeover races, IN_PROGRESS without created_at, unknown status, or the repeat-run-after-corruption case.

Three-way parity is verified bit-for-bit with clean porcelain on both ends. CI success is confirmed on the head SHA with a Windows matrix job added. Ghost scan exits 0 with gitignored-path coverage. The B3 module spec now resolves (`orchestrator/run_pipeline.py --help` exit 0), though this was not proven under the cron environment (cwd, PYTHONPATH, interpreter) that produced the original ModuleNotFoundError. The OCR scan covered only 5 of 37 changed files. The golden ffprobe telemetry is acceptable under the declared no-render scope waiver but was truncated.

observations: The packet's own raw evidence falsifies two narrative claims: S05 'exit 0' (actual exit 1) and 'Minimum VN-Hour Policy preserves the morning window' (the 2026-10-16 lock is live and the dry-run skips EN). Rule 121 requires raw evidence to govern over narrative.

Incident 1 (06:21 VN episode created, Gate 1 sent, B3 crash) followed by Incident 2 (15:29 VN full re-crawl) is the defining failure. The guard's recognition sources are lock, registry, and episode run_manifest. A B3 crash leaves no manifest and possibly no lock, and registry detection depends on recorded_at and task_id semantics that are not shown. A regression test replaying this exact sequence is missing.

The fail-closed semantics are inconsistent across the two new modules. alert_cooldown raises on write failure while daily_market_lock returns False, and corruption handling quarantines and then effectively re-opens on the next tick. A single policy is needed: persistent fail-closed via a CORRUPT marker that survives until operator action or --force.

Duplicated cleanup_corrupt_quarantines (near byte-identical in both modules) plus divergent atomic-write helpers violate Rule 125 single truth. Both should live in one core utility (e.g. core/atomic_io.py) next to core.paths.resolve_state_dir.

The commit range 96f6483..HEAD spans at least two task IDs (AVF-VOX-001 and TASK_1792069373) plus tooling and SKILL.md edits. This inflates blast radius and prevents a clean per-task audit (Rule 124 atomicity).

The cooldown file key `b1_viability::EN` reports suppressions over a fixed '4h' label even when suppressions span longer windows. With 27 test-origin suppressions, the next operator alert will be misleading.
